scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: Hello, I'm on PC0 (20.1.1.x). I can't get through to
PC12 (120.1.1.x) on the far side of the network any more -- it times out
every time. I vaguely remember hearing our two sides run on "different
routing" somehow, but I honestly don't know what that means. Could someone
take a look at whatever connects the two sides and fix it? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully healthy. There is no fault present.

PC0 (20.1.1.10) and PC12 (120.1.1.10) communicate via a correctly configured two-domain routing boundary. The OSPF domain covers r1 through r10 (areas 0 and 3), while the EIGRP AS 100 domain covers r12 and r13. Router r11 acts as the redistribution boundary: it runs both OSPF (on the 111.0.0.0/8 segment connecting to r1) and EIGRP (on the 112.0.0.0/8 segment connecting to r12 and 103.0.0.0/8 connecting to r13). Its configuration correctly carries `redistribute eigrp` inside the OSPF process, so r12's 120.0.0.0/8 network is flooded into OSPF as a Type-5 external LSA (confirmed present in the OSPF database on both r11 and r1). The reverse path uses a kernel default route on r12 (default via 112.1.1.1) pointing back to r11, which then forwards to r1 via the OSPF-learned 20.0.0.0/8 route.

All OSPF adjacencies have been in Full state for over 7 minutes. Both EIGRP neighbor pairs (r11↔r12, r11↔r13) are established. No iptables rules exist on any device in the path. IP forwarding is enabled on all routers. FRR logs on r11, r12, and r1 show only clean startup events with no flaps or daemon restarts. Direct ping tests — both PC0→PC12 and PC12→PC0 at 5 packets — confirm 0% packet loss and consistent sub-2ms RTT. The user's report that the path "times out every time" does not match any observable network condition.

Corrective action: None required. The topology and routing configuration are operating as designed.
